subject: Service Interruption — Technical findings, customer verification steps, and compensation offer
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@fintegrate.com>; Anna Li <anna.li@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Service Interruption — Initial technical findings and verification steps

Hi Sam / Anna,

Thanks again for your patience while our team investigated the disruption on 2026-09-02 that impacted embedding and generation requests for customers routed through the us-west-2 cluster. This thread is to share our initial technical findings, the steps we’d like you to run to verify recovery on your side, and the attachments with the timeline + checklist.

Summary (short):
- Impact window: 2026-09-02 14:07:22 UTC — 2026-09-02 15:43:10 UTC (approx).
- Visible customer symptom: elevated token latency and intermittent 5xxs for models served from the shared us-west-2 pool.
- Immediate cause (high level): an autoscaler regression combined with a stale cache eviction policy that caused a cascade of pod restarts under burst load.

What we’ve attached:
- 20260903_timeline.csv — precise event timestamps from our control plane and affected nodes.
- mitigation-checklist.pdf — recommended verification steps for customers (quick checks).

Customer verification steps we’d like you to run now (5–10 minutes):
1) Run a short smoke test at your normal concurrency (3–5 concurrent requests) and capture 50 requests for generation and 50 for embeddings.
2) Share a sample of request IDs (X-Request-ID) if you see >250ms median generation latency or any 5xx.
3) If you still observe problems, toggle your routing to the eu-central-1 fallback (we can apply a temporary routing rule on our side) and report comparative latency.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll provide a concise RCA with technical root cause analysis by EOD tomorrow.
- We will publish a proposed service credit for the impacted window; details in follow up.
- Marcus and Grace are on standby to coordinate verification and any config changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affected production traffic and are treating it with priority. Please run the checklist above and send the sample request IDs if you see any lingering issues.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260903_timeline.csv, mitigation-checklist.pdf

- Sample request IDs (X-Request-ID): rq_9a1c, rq_9a1d, rq_9a1f, rq_9a21, rq_9a2b, rq_9a3c, rq_9a4f.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@fintegrate.com>; Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>; Anna Li <anna.li@fintegrate.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service Interruption — Initial technical findings and verification steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the request IDs, that helped. We correlated those IDs to the timeline and confirmed they all hit pods that restarted due to an autoscaler bug during a rapid scale event. Detail (concise):
- Root cause: a regression in the autoscaler introduced in release v2.14.3 that failed to respect a cold-start grace period. When the fleet experienced a short burst, some pods were marked unhealthy prematurely triggering restarts; the cache eviction policy then forced heavier KV cache repopulation which amplified latency across co-hosted tenants.
- Why it affected your traffic: Fintegrate’s routing policy had a sticky preference to us-west-2 and your traffic profile produced hot prefixes on a small subset of pods during the burst window.

What we changed (already deployed):
1) Rolled back the autoscaler to v2.14.2 on us-west-2 (completed 2026-09-02 16:10 UTC).
2) Applied a targeted cache eviction patch to reduce cold-start pressure (completed 2026-09-02 16:28 UTC).
3) Added a temporary routing rule to move new connections to warm nodes in the us-west-2 reserved pool.

Next corrective actions (commitments):
- Engineering runbook change: add a pre-scale health-hold for future autoscaler changes (targeted deploy 2026-09-12).
- Monitoring: new metric emitted for pod restart chains and KV-cache miss spikes (in staging by 2026-09-07).
- Customer verification: Tessa will coordinate a short verification window with you tomorrow to confirm no residual 5xxs.

Regarding service credit: we propose a one-time service credit equal to 6 hours of provisioned usage for the impacted ingress for the month of September. If Fintegrate prefers a percentage-of-invoice model we can provide that table as well. I’m looping Grace who owns billing credits for final confirmation.

Marcus
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: service-credit-form.pdf

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service Interruption — Technical findings, customer verification steps, and compensation offer

Hi Sam / Anna — quick note from billing & ops:

Thanks for confirming the request IDs and for running the verification checks. We’ve reviewed the timeline and Marcus’s fixes and have prepared the following:

1) Verification outcome: based on your smoke runs and our follow-up checks, there are no remaining 5xxs tied to the September 2 event. If you see anything after the routing warm-up we set, please reply with the X-Request-IDs and we’ll escalate immediately.

2) Service credit offer: we can issue a one-time service credit that covers 6 hours of provisioned capacity for Sept invoice (applies to the account-level invoice). To accept, please complete the attached service-credit-form.pdf and return to contracts@redwood.ai. If procurement requests a different structure (e.g., prorated invoice percentage), we can supply a breakdown.

3) Action items we’ll own (with target dates):
- Engineering: autoscaler hold rule and rollout checklist — complete by 2026-09-12.
- Observability: deploy pod-restart-chain metric to prod monitoring — 2026-09-07 (in progress).
- Customer ops: we will run a one-hour verification session with Fintegrate on 2026-09-08 09:00 PT if that works. Tessa, please confirm scheduling.

4) What we need from Fintegrate: if you have preference on credit format (invoice credit vs. percentage) please loop procurement or return the completed form. Also, please keep sample request IDs for 72 hours in case we need to do a deeper packet-level trace.

Apologies again for the disruption. We appreciate the quick collaboration and will keep you posted as the monitoring changes land.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Billing & Customer Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-credit-form.pdf
